html:
SMTO-TSK-0029 — The task's question or approval has changed

GUID: 2b8235c4-eef4-4d46-8c20-963e189ee355
Slug: task-interaction-changed
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • By the time you replied, the task was asking something different or had already moved on, so SMTO didn't use your reply.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and scroll to the task's latest message to see what it is asking now. Your reply was meant for a question or approval that has changed or was already answered.
  2. If the task asks you to approve an action, use its buttons, Approve once or Deny / stop task, instead of typing a reply. A typed reply never counts as approval for a protected action.
  3. If the task shows choices, select one of them rather than typing a different answer. The task only accepts one of the options it offered you.
  4. If you were running a command from the message box, make sure the right conversation is open, then run it again. The command was stopped because the open conversation changed before it could run.

What success looks like

  • Your reply or approval is accepted and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve an action without reading it again first; the request may have changed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An answer, approval, runtime-guard override or command targeted an interaction that is no longer current: it was already handled or replaced, needs explicit approval rather than an ordinary answer, the answer was not an offered option, or the conversation changed.

What this means

  • The current interaction/approval identity changed or was consumed, a supplied answer is not allowed, an override is no longer applicable, or the selected conversation disappeared. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The current interaction/approval identity changed or was consumed, a supplied answer is not allowed, an override is no longer applicable, or the selected conversation disappeared.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh pending question/approval/guard state and exact operation identity; an ordinary answer cannot approve a protected action.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the run's pending interaction (question, unsafe-action approval or runtime-guard override) and its operation identity, then answer only the current interaction with one of its offered options. Protected actions require the explicit approval control; an ordinary answer never grants approval.
  • Refresh the task and respond through its current interaction controls. Use explicit approval controls for a protected action; an ordinary answer does not grant approval.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching current interaction accepts the intended response through its own authority boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
